knowledge_point.title: Calculating a Line Integral Along a Segment in the Cartesian Plane

question.:question/problem: Evaluate the integral of the function $f(x,y)=2 x + 2 y$ along the line segment from $(3,-3)$ to $(3,0)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\int_C f(x,y)\,\mathrm{d}s=\int_{t_a}^{t_b} f(r(t))\,\|r\prime(t)\|\,\mathrm{d}t,
$$

where $C$ is the line segment from $(3,-3)$ to $(3,0).$

The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are $a=(3)\,i+(-3)\,j$ and $b=(3)\,i+(0)\,j.$ So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t\,(b-a) \\  & =(3)\,i+(-3)\,j+t((0)\,i+(3)\,j) \\  & =(3)\,i+(3 \cdot t - 3)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

where $0\le t\le 1.$ Thus, we have that $x=3$ and $y=3 \cdot t - 3$ along the segment.

Computing $r\prime(t)$ and $\|r\prime(t)\|,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}r\prime(t) & =\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}\,i+\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(3)i+\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(3 \cdot t - 3)j \\  & =(0)\,i+(3)\,j \\ \|r\prime(t)\| & =\sqrt{\left(\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}\right)^2} \\  & =\sqrt{(0)^2+(3)^2} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)=2 \cdot x + 2 \cdot y$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =2(3)+2(3 \cdot t - 3) \\  & =6 \cdot t.\end{aligned}
$$

Write $I=\int_C f(x,y)\,\mathrm{d}s$. Then

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =\int_0^1 f(r(t))\,\|r\prime(t)\|\,\mathrm{d}t \\  & =\int_0^1 (6 \cdot t)\cdot 3\,\mathrm{d}t \\  & =3\int_0^1 (6 \cdot t)\,\mathrm{d}t \\  & =3[3 \cdot t^{2}]_0^1 \\  & =3((3)+(0))-3(0) \\  & =9\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Evaluate the integral of the function $f(x,y)=\left(6 x + 9\right) e^{x y}$ along the line segment from $(-1,3)$ to $(1,6)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\int_C f(x,y)\,\mathrm{d}s=\int_{t_a}^{t_b} f(r(t))\,\|r\prime(t)\|\,\mathrm{d}t,
$$

where $C$ is the line segment from $(-1,3)$ to $(1,6).$

The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are $a=(-1)\,i+(3)\,j$ and $b=(1)\,i+(6)\,j.$ So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t\,(b-a) \\  & =(-1)\,i+(3)\,j+t((2)\,i+(3)\,j) \\  & =(2 \cdot t - 1)\,i+(3 \cdot t + 3)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

where $0\le t\le 1.$ Thus, we have that $x=2 \cdot t - 1$ and $y=3 \cdot t + 3$ along the segment.

Computing $r\prime(t)$ and $\|r\prime(t)\|,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}r\prime(t) & =\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}\,i+\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(2 \cdot t - 1)i+\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(3 \cdot t + 3)j \\  & =(2)\,i+(3)\,j \\ \|r\prime(t)\| & =\sqrt{\left(\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}\right)^2} \\  & =\sqrt{(2)^2+(3)^2} \\  & =\sqrt{13}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)=\left(6 \cdot x + 9\right) \cdot e^{x \cdot y}$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =(6(2 \cdot t - 1)+9)e^{(2 \cdot t - 1)(3 \cdot t + 3)} \\  & =(12 \cdot t + 3)e^{6 \cdot t^{2} + 3 \cdot t - 3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Write $I=\int_C f(x,y)\,\mathrm{d}s$. Then

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =\int_0^1 f(r(t))\,\|r\prime(t)\|\,\mathrm{d}t \\  & =\int_0^1 ((12 \cdot t + 3)e^{6 \cdot t^{2} + 3 \cdot t - 3})\cdot \sqrt{13}\,\mathrm{d}t \\  & =\sqrt{13}\int_0^1 ((12 \cdot t + 3)e^{6 \cdot t^{2} + 3 \cdot t - 3})\,\mathrm{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this using the substitution $u=6 \cdot t^{2} + 3 \cdot t - 3,$ $\mathrm{d}u=(12 \cdot t + 3)\,\mathrm{d}t$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =\sqrt{13}\int_{-3}^{6}e^u\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\sqrt{13}[e^u]_{-3}^{6} \\  & =\sqrt{13}(e^{6}-e^{-3}) \\  & =\sqrt{13} \cdot \left(- \frac{1}{e^{3}} + e^{6}\right)\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Evaluate the integral of the function $f(x,y)=\sec^{2}{\left(\frac{\pi \left(- x + y\right)}{4} \right)}$ along the line segment from $(1,1)$ to $(-1,0)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\int_C f(x,y)\,\mathrm{d}s=\int_{t_a}^{t_b} f(r(t))\,\|r\prime(t)\|\,\mathrm{d}t,
$$

where $C$ is the line segment from $(1,1)$ to $(-1,0).$

The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are $a=(1)\,i+(1)\,j$ and $b=(-1)\,i+(0)\,j.$ So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t\,(b-a) \\  & =(1)\,i+(1)\,j+t((-2)\,i+(-1)\,j) \\  & =(1 - 2 \cdot t)\,i+(1 - t)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

where $0\le t\le 1.$ Thus, we have that $x=1 - 2 \cdot t$ and $y=1 - t$ along the segment.

Computing $r\prime(t)$ and $\|r\prime(t)\|,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}r\prime(t) & =\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}\,i+\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(1 - 2 \cdot t)i+\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(1 - t)j \\  & =(-2)\,i+(-1)\,j \\ \|r\prime(t)\| & =\sqrt{\left(\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}\right)^2} \\  & =\sqrt{(-2)^2+(-1)^2} \\  & =\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)=\sec^{2}{\left(\frac{\pi \cdot \left(- x + y\right)}{4} \right)}$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =\sec^2\left(\frac{\pi((1 - t)-(1 - 2 \cdot t))}{4}\right) \\  & =\sec^2\left(\frac{\pi \cdot t}{4}\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Write $I=\int_C f(x,y)\,\mathrm{d}s$. Then

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =\int_0^1 f(r(t))\,\|r\prime(t)\|\,\mathrm{d}t \\  & =\int_0^1 (\sec^2\left(\frac{\pi \cdot t}{4}\right))\cdot \sqrt{5}\,\mathrm{d}t \\  & =\sqrt{5}\int_0^1 (\sec^2\left(\frac{\pi \cdot t}{4}\right))\,\mathrm{d}t\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this using the substitution $u=\frac{\pi \cdot t}{4},$ $\mathrm{d}u=\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\,\mathrm{d}t$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =\frac{4 \cdot \sqrt{5}}{\pi}\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{4}}\sec^2 u\,\mathrm{d}u \\  & =\frac{4 \cdot \sqrt{5}}{\pi}[\tan u]_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \\  & =\frac{4 \cdot \sqrt{5}}{\pi}(\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)-\tan(0)) \\  & =\frac{4 \cdot \sqrt{5}}{\pi}(1-0) \\  & =\frac{4 \cdot \sqrt{5}}{\pi}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Evaluate the integral of the function $f(x,y)=e^{- x + y}$ along the line segment from $(0,0)$ to $(1,4)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\int_C f(x,y)\,\mathrm{d}s=\int_{t_a}^{t_b} f(r(t))\,\|r\prime(t)\|\,\mathrm{d}t,
$$

where $C$ is the line segment from $(0,0)$ to $(1,4).$

The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are $a=(0)\,i+(0)\,j$ and $b=(1)\,i+(4)\,j.$ So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t\,(b-a) \\  & =(0)\,i+(0)\,j+t((1)\,i+(4)\,j) \\  & =(t)\,i+(4 \cdot t)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

where $0\le t\le 1.$ Thus, we have that $x=t$ and $y=4 \cdot t$ along the segment.

Computing $r\prime(t)$ and $\|r\prime(t)\|,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}r\prime(t) & =\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}\,i+\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(t)i+\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(4 \cdot t)j \\  & =(1)\,i+(4)\,j \\ \|r\prime(t)\| & =\sqrt{\left(\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}\right)^2} \\  & =\sqrt{(1)^2+(4)^2} \\  & =\sqrt{17}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)=e^{- x + y}$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =e^{-1(t)+1(4 \cdot t)} \\  & =e^{3 \cdot t}.\end{aligned}
$$

The exponent has derivative $3$. With $u=3 t$, $\mathrm{d}u=3\,\mathrm{d}t$; the new bounds are $0$ and $3$. Write $I=\int_C f(x,y)\,\mathrm{d}s$. Then

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =\int_0^1 f(r(t))\,\|r\prime(t)\|\,\mathrm{d}t \\  & =\int_0^1 (e^{3 \cdot t})\cdot \sqrt{17}\,\mathrm{d}t \\  & =\sqrt{17}\int_0^1 (e^{3 \cdot t})\,\mathrm{d}t \\  & =\sqrt{17}[\frac{e^{3 \cdot t}}{3}]_0^1 \\  & =\sqrt{17}\left(\frac{e^{3}}{3}\right)-\sqrt{17}\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) \\  & =\sqrt{17} \cdot \left(- \frac{1}{3} + \frac{e^{3}}{3}\right)\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Evaluate the integral of the function $f(x,y)=2 x y$ along the line segment from $(2,-2)$ to $(4,-1)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\int_C f(x,y)\,\mathrm{d}s=\int_{t_a}^{t_b} f(r(t))\,\|r\prime(t)\|\,\mathrm{d}t,
$$

where $C$ is the line segment from $(2,-2)$ to $(4,-1).$

The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are $a=(2)\,i+(-2)\,j$ and $b=(4)\,i+(-1)\,j.$ So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t\,(b-a) \\  & =(2)\,i+(-2)\,j+t((2)\,i+(1)\,j) \\  & =(2 \cdot t + 2)\,i+(t - 2)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

where $0\le t\le 1.$ Thus, we have that $x=2 \cdot t + 2$ and $y=t - 2$ along the segment.

Computing $r\prime(t)$ and $\|r\prime(t)\|,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}r\prime(t) & =\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}\,i+\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(2 \cdot t + 2)i+\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(t - 2)j \\  & =(2)\,i+(1)\,j \\ \|r\prime(t)\| & =\sqrt{\left(\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}\right)^2} \\  & =\sqrt{(2)^2+(1)^2} \\  & =\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)=2 \cdot x \cdot y$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =2(2 \cdot t + 2)(t - 2) \\  & =4 \cdot t^{2} - 4 \cdot t - 8.\end{aligned}
$$

Write $I=\int_C f(x,y)\,\mathrm{d}s$. Then

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =\int_0^1 f(r(t))\,\|r\prime(t)\|\,\mathrm{d}t \\  & =\int_0^1 (4 \cdot t^{2} - 4 \cdot t - 8)\cdot \sqrt{5}\,\mathrm{d}t \\  & =\sqrt{5}\int_0^1 (4 \cdot t^{2} - 4 \cdot t - 8)\,\mathrm{d}t \\  & =\sqrt{5}[\frac{4 \cdot t^{3}}{3} - 2 \cdot t^{2} - 8 \cdot t]_0^1 \\  & =\sqrt{5}(\left(\frac{4}{3}\right)+(-2)+(-8))-\sqrt{5}(0) \\  & =- \frac{26 \cdot \sqrt{5}}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Evaluate the integral of the function $f(x,y)=x + \sqrt{2} \sqrt{y}$ along the line segment from $(3,0)$ to $(3,8)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\int_C f(x,y)\,\mathrm{d}s=\int_{t_a}^{t_b} f(r(t))\,\|r\prime(t)\|\,\mathrm{d}t,
$$

where $C$ is the line segment from $(3,0)$ to $(3,8).$

The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are $a=(3)\,i+(0)\,j$ and $b=(3)\,i+(8)\,j.$ So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t\,(b-a) \\  & =(3)\,i+(0)\,j+t((0)\,i+(8)\,j) \\  & =(3)\,i+(8 \cdot t)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

where $0\le t\le 1.$ Thus, we have that $x=3$ and $y=8 \cdot t$ along the segment.

Computing $r\prime(t)$ and $\|r\prime(t)\|,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}r\prime(t) & =\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}\,i+\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(3)i+\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(8 \cdot t)j \\  & =(0)\,i+(8)\,j \\ \|r\prime(t)\| & =\sqrt{\left(\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}\right)^2} \\  & =\sqrt{(0)^2+(8)^2} \\  & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)=x + \sqrt{2} \cdot \sqrt{y}$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =3+\sqrt{2(8 \cdot t)} \\  & =4 \cdot \sqrt{t} + 3.\end{aligned}
$$

Write $I=\int_C f(x,y)\,\mathrm{d}s$. Then

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =\int_0^1 f(r(t))\,\|r\prime(t)\|\,\mathrm{d}t \\  & =\int_0^1 (4 \cdot \sqrt{t} + 3)\cdot 8\,\mathrm{d}t \\  & =24\int_0^1 (\frac{4 \cdot \sqrt{t}}{3} + 1)\,\mathrm{d}t \\  & =24[\frac{8 \cdot t^{\frac{3}{2}}}{9} + t]_0^1 \\  & =24(1+\frac{8}{9})-0 \\  & =\frac{136}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
